In the Friday salat the final yeh of both words has no shadda+kasra, unlike النَّبِيِّ الأُمِّيِّ in the second bullet. Kept as printed.
The yeh has only a kasra and no shadda (expected السَّيِّئَاتِ). Checked at 1800 dpi.
The lam has only a kasra and no shadda (expected وَتُبَلِّغُنَا). Checked at 1500 dpi.
The kasra marks are under the jeem and the medial heh, and the final heh has none (expected بِوَجْهِهِ). Checked at 2600 dpi.
A sukun is printed over the yeh. Kept.
In the heading the shadda+kasra sit on the ص and the د is bare (expected الصِّدِّيقي).
The meem has a shadda with no fatha. Kept.
A fatha is printed on the ك (expected كُلِّ). Checked at 2400 dpi.
A kasra is printed under the ي (expected أَمْسَيْتُ). Checked at 2400 dpi.
The د has no kasra (expected سَيِّدِنَا).
The final ك of وَحْدَك has no fatha, but the other ك in the line have one. Kept.
A space is printed before the closing ornate bracket. Written glued (CONVENTIONS §2). The reference «[الأعراف:٨٩]» is printed with no space after the colon and is kept that way.
The fatha stands over the ر and the ت is bare (expected أَقْتَرِفَ). Checked at 3600 dpi.
The و has no fatha. Kept.
In «فاطر السماوات والأرض» the hamza has no fatha. The later «فِي الأَرْض» has a fatha on the hamza but no vowel on the ض. Both kept as printed.
The lam has no shadda (expected الَّتِي). Kept.

notes: p049 opens with the # heading after p048's complete list, so there is no '+'. p048 has no footnotes, so there is no (تابع). The pages 050, 051 and 052 each start a new indented paragraph after a complete sentence, so none has a '+'. Bullets are printed as a flower asterisk and written '* ' (CONVENTIONS §7, STRUCTURE). The word الله: wherever the plain font ligature is used, it is written الله, and only a separately printed case fatha is added (اللهَ on p049 and p052), as in earlier keyB batches (b12 اللهِ). Final ى carrying the font's automatic small alif is written as plain ى (عَلَى، إلى، ترضى، مَضَى، تُقْضَى، أَقْصَى، إِلَى). p050: the Tazi salat line «اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ صَلاةً…» starts flush right with no indent, and the line before it («…وصيغتها بالتلقي:») is full width. Per §6 it is joined to the «في الملمات…» paragraph. In the same way, on p051 «أربع مرات.» is joined to the preceding dua, and the reference «[الأعراف:٨٩].», which wraps onto its own line, stays with the Quran quotation. p050 «وتقسم على جميع الحاضرين.» is a bold standalone instruction, written as a **bold** paragraph. p051: the paragraph «يُقْرَأُ مرة في الصباح…» under the title is set in bold, but per STRUCTURE §2 a «تقرأ…» line under a title is a plain paragraph, so no ** was used. The calligraphic basmala is written in the standard form outside the brackets. The Quran text (الأعراف ٨٩) matches Tanzil with no tatweel before the dagger alif. In the lam-alif ligature the hamza of لأ sits on the left slanted stroke, which identifies that stroke as the alif. The fathatan above that stroke in «أَعْمَالاً» (p051) is therefore encoded on the alif. «لَمْ يَشَأ لَمْ يَكُنْ» (p052) is set tight, but each word is written separately with a space. All lines were checked against 650 dpi half-line renders and 1300 dpi third-line renders, plus 1500–3600 dpi zooms of every questionable mark (scratch\b13_*.png).
